# Charter — T13 Tool platform (retrospective, 2026-11-22)

- **Project:** T13 "Tool platform", track v2, ADM phase G, plateau capability, tranche 3, issue #76. Measured status `built`; this charter is authored retrospectively from SPEC_V2 §11 and the proving suite, and the project is **not** closed here.
- **Sponsor and accepting owner:** the programme owner, named in the rework decision document. The architecture board decides the SoAW and the delivery contract under the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`; requester and approver are distinct identities.
- **Purpose:** give every conveyor-internal run exactly one governed way to reach a job backend — `tools.call` — with the binding row as its authority, refusal before dispatch, one `tool_call` ledger row per call, credential brokerage over sealed secrets, and tenant-prefixed object storage.
- **Scope, in:** the broker `tools.call`; the `tool`, `toolkit`, `tool_binding` and `tool_call` tables; effect classes read/write/destructive/spend; binding-scoped credential aliases; the direct MinIO storage adapter with the `tenant/<tenant_id>/` prefix; the coding toolkit and one kag-era toolkit; V1's external actions migrated onto toolkit operations and `artifacts.list` onto the storage adapter; the six §12 gate proofs.
- **Scope, out:** the catalogue actions and the estate import (T14); the agent platform gateway `nonagenticai_mcp_server` (D44/D59 — two paths permanently); the BYO publication surface (gap ledger v1-w4a-6); live MinIO wiring (v1-p1110-1); a production `tool_binding` writer (v1-p111-1).
- **Success:** the manifest's gate, `acceptance/programme/T13.toml`, proved by the six named tests in `crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs`; each proof is a wire assertion against a counting HTTP stub, not an error-string assertion.
- **Constraints that shaped it:** one repository, one schema, one queue; the prompt and the ledger never carry a credential; the destination is a registered alias, never a caller-supplied URL; `tool_call` is not `action_invocation` and a call never transitions a card.
- **Why the closure is withheld:** five honest findings below (no production binding writer, test-only storage path, destructive execution path unproved, kag-era/V1 migration unexercised, and the sub-features listed in v1-w4a-5/v1-p111-3/v1-p118-2/v1-w4a-6) must be disposed or waived through the delegated chain first.

input.body:
# Statement of Architecture Work — T13 Tool platform

## Context
SPEC_V2 §11 replaces ad-hoc backend calls with one governed path. The conveyor already owns actions, secrets, entitlements, audit and a durable queue, so a second catalogue/queue/runner (the predecessor MCP server) is refused (D44, D59). T13 is the slice that makes the one path real.

## Scope
The broker `tools.call` and its seven steps; the four catalogue/ledger tables; effect-class gating; the closed-schema input check; credential aliases over sealed secrets; the direct MinIO storage adapter with the mandatory tenant prefix; the coding toolkit and one kag-era toolkit; V1 external-action migration; six gate proofs.

## Approach
Implement the broker and storage layers in the conveyor workspace, prove each refusal before dispatch at the wire (a counting stub), record one `tool_call` and one `tool.called` event per call, and record every artefact of this rework retrospectively from §11 and the tests rather than from memory.

## Deliverables
`crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs` (the six proofs and the extra broker tests); `conveyor_actions::storage::{JobStorage, TENANT_PREFIX, sha256_hex}`; `conveyor_store::tool::{calls_for_run, ToolCallRow}`; `conveyor_actions::prompt::compile_for_audit`; the reused `conveyor_store::secret::create_secret_tx`; tables `tool`, `toolkit`, `tool_binding`, `tool_call`; action `tools.call`; event `tool.called`.

## Constraints and standards
Rust workspace; PostgreSQL 18; MinIO (S3-compatible) as the platform store; a closed JSON-Schema subset (additionalProperties false, enums, patterns, bounds); OpenAPI 3.1 and streamable-HTTP MCP as the only two BYO forms; idempotency keys on writes and bounded polls.

## Acceptance
The six §12 clauses and their named tests, as written in `acceptance/programme/T13.toml`; the manifest is the gate, not this document.

## Risks
The suite serialises because the destination URL is process-global; the storage test path is test-only until live MinIO wiring exists; the catalogue write path is deferred to T14; a production binding writer is still absent.

## Decisions closed by this rework
The binding row is the broker's authority; refusals are proved on the wire; `tool_call` is not `action_invocation`; the storage adapter builds every key, so traversal and hash mismatches are refused.

# Delivery contract — T13 Tool platform (retrospective, 2026-11-22)

**Scope.** IN: the broker tools.call; tool, toolkit, tool_binding and tool_call; effect classes read/write/destructive/spend; binding-scoped credential aliases over sealed secrets; the direct MinIO storage adapter with the tenant prefix; the coding toolkit and one kag-era toolkit; V1's external actions migrated onto toolkit operations and artifacts.list onto the storage adapter; the six T13 gate proofs. OUT: catalogue actions and the estate import (T14); the agent platform gateway nonagenticai_mcp_server (D44/D59); BYO publication surface (gap ledger v1-w4a-6); live MinIO wiring (v1-p1110-1); a production tool_binding writer (v1-p111-1).

**Assignment.** Project T13 "Tool platform", issue #76, depends on T2, spec SPEC_V2 §11.1-§11.10, SPEC_V2 §12 T13, plan status authorised (tranche 3).

**Acceptance criteria.** The §12 gate, per clause:

a. A development job calls coding through the broker, not nonagenticai_mcp_server. *Proof:* a_bound_job_calls_coding_through_the_broker: 200; exactly one stub hit; output path /api/jobs via the registered coding destination alias.
b. A tool_call is recorded. *Proof:* one_call_is_one_ledger_row: exactly one row for one call, tool_key coding.jobs.create, toolkit version 1, status ok, http_status 200, 64-hex sha256 input hash, latency; exactly one tool.called event.
c. A destructive call without the tenant's configured approvals is refused. *Proof:* a_destructive_call_without_approvals_is_refused: 403 approval_required; zero destination hits; no tool_call row.
d. Schema-invalid input is refused before the backend call. *Proof:* a_closed_schema_refuses_before_the_call: 422 tool_input_invalid with populated errors[] for an undeclared property, a pattern violation and a numeric bound; zero destination hits; a valid document returns 200 and reaches the destination.
e. A job writes and reads a tenant-prefixed object. *Proof:* a_job_round_trips_a_tenant_prefixed_object: key starts tenant/<tenant_id>/; sha256 matches; read-back bytes match; a wrong hash is refused; head finds the object; a traversal name is refused.
f. The compiled prompt carries no S3 key. *Proof:* the_compiled_prompt_carries_no_s3_key: compiled copilot_system@1 contains none of the access-key, secret-key or CONVEYOR_S3_ sentinels.

**Responsibilities.**

- **T13 delivery** — Ship the broker tools.call, the four catalogue/ledger tables, credential-alias resolution, the tenant-prefixed storage adapter and the proving tests.
- **T2** — Supplies the run and durable-queue context; tool_binding.run_id targets a run, and §12 places T13 after T2.
- **T14** — Owns the estate import; this slice ships no catalogue actions, per the test header.
- **Coding fleet owner** — Registers and reviews the coding destination alias; no caller-supplied URL is admitted at call time (§11.3 step 5).
- **Tenant admins** — Configure destructive-call approvals (§11.4) and approve BYO toolkit publication (§11.5).
- **Platform operator** — Publishes immutable versions, runs tools.probe and retires zero-call tools (§11.6, §11.9).

**Manifest.** The storage, tool and prompt entries are symbol references read from the tests, not independently opened file paths. No migration filename or source pin is asserted because none was read. Adds tables tool, toolkit, tool_binding, tool_call; action tools.call; event tool.called.

**Retrospective.** Authored from §11 and the six proving tests; no gate run is recorded in this record. The tests write tool rows directly because the slice ships no catalogue actions. Decisions closed: the binding row is the broker's authority; refusals are asserted on the wire through the stub counter; tool_call is not action_invocation; the storage adapter builds every key, so traversal names and hash mismatches are refused. Traps to carry: the destination URL is process-global, so the suite serialises; the storage test uses the in-memory store when no endpoint is configured; a production binding writer and the estate import remain outside this slice.

# Project brief — T13 Tool platform (retrospective, 2026-11-22)

## Outcome
Every conveyor-internal run reaches a job backend through `tools.call` under a binding row's authority, with effect, budget and schema decided before any network call and exactly one `tool_call` row and one `tool.called` event per call.

## Boundary
Out of scope: the catalogue actions and the estate import (T14); the agent platform gateway `nonagenticai_mcp_server` (D44/D59); the BYO publication surface (v1-w4a-6); live MinIO wiring (v1-p1110-1); a production `tool_binding` writer (v1-p111-1). The slice must not fork T2's run/queue or T14's import.

## Reuse sources
- `conveyor_store::secret::create_secret_tx` — sealed credentials, reused rather than rebuilt (§11.8).
- `event` and `audit_event` — the call event and audit trail (§11.3 step 7).
- `governed_asset(kind='tool_draft')` — the publication lifecycle (§11.6).
- T2's run and durable queue — `tool_binding.run_id` targets a run (§12).

## Inception units
The analysis T13 starts with is SPEC_V2 §11.1–§11.10 and the §12 T13 row; both are the basis of every artefact in this record.

## Dependencies
- blocked-by: T2 (run and queue context).
- related: T14 (estate import, out of this slice), P0 (constitution and gates).

## Acceptance
The §12 gate: a development job calls coding through the broker; a `tool_call` is recorded; a destructive call without approvals is refused; schema-invalid input is refused before the backend call; a job writes and reads a tenant-prefixed object; the compiled prompt carries no S3 key — proved by six named tests, re-run for this record (tool_platform 17/17 passed at lane head 582e2dc6 (2026-11-22), against a fresh Postgres 18 and a counting HTTP stub).

## Capabilities
Broker dispatch, effect-class and budget gating, closed-schema input enforcement, credential-alias brokerage, the call ledger, and tenant-separated object storage, as the Phase-B capability map records.

## Plan
The WBS deliverable "the tool platform — one governed call path, the call ledger, the schema and effect gates, and tenant-prefixed storage", accepted with this record; the open items are carried to the tranche review.

# Evidence — T13 Tool platform (retrospective, 2026-11-22)

## Claim
The T13 slice implements §11's broker, ledger, gates and storage adapter, and the six §12 clauses are proved by named wire-level tests.

## Evidence
- `crates/actions/tests/tool_platform.rs` — 17 tests, re-run for this record: tool_platform 17/17 passed at lane head 582e2dc6 (2026-11-22), against a fresh Postgres 18 and a counting HTTP stub.
- `acceptance/programme/T13.toml` — the gate the tests serve.
- The seven A–D artefacts, the Statement of Architecture Work and the delivery contract recorded in this retrospective batch.

## Verification
Run the tool_platform suite through the build guard at the recorded sha; the suite needs a fresh Postgres 18 and starts a counting HTTP stub, so a refusal that called upstream moves the counter and fails.

## Links
